text: Bath is a British site of note for its hot springs. The town lies in south-west England, twelve miles south-east of Bristol. People have known its healing waters since prehistoric times. The Romans called the place Aquae Sulis. They took the name of the Celtic deity Sul and merged her with Minerva. They built temples and baths that still stand. The Celtic custom of tossing offerings into water was observed at Bath. People also engraved curses on sheets of lead. Excavation has recovered more than 16,000 coins and over 50 cursing tables. In Welsh the town is called Caer Faddon. Writers including Gildas, Bede, and the Historia Brittonum link the town to the battle of Mount Badon. In Old English it carried the names Hat Bathu and at Badhum, which refer to the Roman baths.
